search.title: LEA14
search.description: This part encodes a Late Embryogenesis Abundant 14 protein (LEA14) from *Arabidopsis thaliana* gene *At1g01470.1*, which belongs to LEA\_2 subgroup. The paper showed overexpression of AtLEA14 enhances salt stress tolerance in *Arabidopsis thaliana*. Therefore, LEA14 is might be the potential gene involved in plant responses to abiotic stress. The LEA14 coding sequence was codon-optimized for *B. subtilis*.

## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 

## Dry lab / computational analysis

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/bd1cc363-e134-4fb0-ab15-ff12e192d1b6/d087c7afc2e99e4daa3db1f3e52546067d5affb31740b0a34ba7d193d2b92ddb.avif)

**Figure ST-2. LEA14, a β-sandwich with a disordered N-terminal arm.** (a) The LEA14 fold, from PDB 1XO8 model 1 (solution NMR, 20 models, O03983 (LEA14\_ARATH)). Residues residues 2–151 of this structure are exactly the mature protein our cassette encodes — the structure is of our own protein, not a homologue. The core is a 9-stranded β-sandwich with one helix (residues 98–112); the N-terminal 16 residues, orange, carry no fixed structure. (b) The same molecule coloured and thickened by per-residue RMSF across all 20 deposited models, superposed on CA 28-143. The contrast is the point: the core (residues 28–143) averages 0.42 Å, while the N-terminal 1–16 averages 8.75 Å and reaches 11.9 Å. Residues 17–27 are already ordered at 1.13 Å, which is where order actually begins. LEA14 is a late-embryogenesis-abundant protein that protects membranes and enzymes against the water loss that comes with salt and drought stress.

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **LEA14 2.1** ([<u>BBa\_26IN6G1D</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26in6g1d)): In this variant, the first 15 codons of the LEA14 coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.
* **Csn-LEA14-Histag** ([<u>BBa\_26ZQ1T72</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zq1t72)): The Late Embryogenesis Abundant (LEA14) protein is fused to the chitosanase signal (Csn) peptide at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus.
* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-LEA14-Histag-B0015** ([<u>BBa\_26SG0NQQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26sg0nqq)): this Protectant Module constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS0, and terminator B0015.
